sources.entry: Monolingual - Remove unnecessary language resources from macOS

summary.one_liner: Monolingual is a macOS app that deletes unneeded language localization files and unused architecture slices from installed applications to free disk space.
summary.what_it_does: The app scans folders (by default /Applications and /Library) and lets you choose language resources and architecture slices to remove. A privileged helper, registered as a launch daemon via Service Management (SMAppService), performs the deletions and talks to the app over XPC. Removals show progress in a sheet with the current file and space freed so far, can be cancelled, and send a notification with the space saved. The language and architecture lists have a search field that filters as you type. English language files cannot be selected for removal. Updates use Sparkle 2 with EdDSA-signed releases. The README also describes a bundled lipo tool built with swift-argument-parser.
use_cases: free disk space by removing unused app languages
strip unneeded architectures from universal binaries
thin macOS applications to save storage
remove unwanted localization files from Mac apps
clean up old language packs on a Mac
how_to_run: Release packaging (signing, notarization, disk image): make release
notable: Privileged helper registered as a launch daemon with SMAppService, approved once in System Settings
Refuses to remove English language files, which would break macOS
Search field filters the language and architecture lists as you type
Localized into 17 languages, kept in a String Catalog
Notarized app with EdDSA-signed Sparkle updates
caveats: Requires macOS 27 on Apple silicon, per the README
Needs an administrator to approve the helper in System Settings › General › Login Items & Extensions before it can run
The app is no longer sandboxed, so settings from 2.0 do not carry over and added folders must be re-added
